FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion. There is significant soft tissue swelling surrounding the knee.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is thickening and increased signal involving the distal posterior cruciate ligament with partial tear (approximately 50% of the fibers) of the posterior medial fibers. There is mild thickening and increased signal involving the proximal and mid aspect of the PCL.

There is complete radial tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is unremarkable.

There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament with distal avulsion of the superficial component which is retracted proximally and superficial to the pes anserine tendons compatible with a pseudoStener lesion. There is also high-grade injury involving the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial component of the MCL with thickening of the posterior oblique ligament.

There is almost complete tear of the lateral collateral ligament at its femoral attachment. There are thinned out fibers that appear physically continuous. This is likely a functionally complete tear. There is also almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon as it courses around the lateral femoral condyle with significant thinning and laxity of the tendon. There is disruption of the popliteal fibular ligament. The distal biceps femoris insertion remains intact.

There is significant bone marrow edema at the posterior tibial plateau fractures. There is also bone contusion involving the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and minimal contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an enchondroma in the distal femur.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL with a moderate grade injury of the PCL.

2. High-grade injury involving the medial collateral ligament including distal avulsion of the superficial MCL with pseudo Stener lesion.

3. High-grade tear of the lateral collateral ligament which is likely functionally complete.

4. Almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon. Injury to the popliteal fibular ligament.

5. Complete radial tear involving the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.

6. Significant bone marrow edema surrounding the known tibial plateau fracture with a bone contusion in the lateral femoral condyle.

7. large knee joint effusion.

all_changed_states.draft_evidence:
FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion. There is significant soft tissue swelling surrounding the knee.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is thickening and increased signal involving the distal posterior cruciate ligament with partial tear (approximately 50% of the fibers) of the posterior medial fibers. There is mild thickening and increased signal involving the proximal and mid aspect of the PCL.

There is complete radial tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is unremarkable.

There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament with distal avulsion of the superficial component which is retracted proximally and superficial to the pes anserine tendons compatible with a pseudoStener lesion. There is also high-grade injury involving the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial component of the MCL with thickening of the posterior oblique ligament.

There is almost complete tear of the lateral collateral ligament at its femoral attachment. There are thinned out fibers that appear physically continuous. This is likely a functionally complete tear. There is also almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon as it courses around the lateral femoral condyle with significant thinning and laxity of the tendon. There is disruption of the popliteal fibular ligament. The distal biceps femoris insertion remains intact.

There is significant bone marrow edema at the posterior tibial plateau fractures. There is also bone contusion involving the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and minimal contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an enchondroma in the distal femur.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL with a moderate grade injury of the PCL.

2. High-grade injury involving the medial collateral ligament including distal avulsion of the superficial MCL with pseudo Stener lesion.

3. High-grade tear of the lateral collateral ligament which is likely functionally complete.

4. Almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon. Injury to the popliteal fibular ligament.

5. Complete radial tear involving the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.

6. Significant bone marrow edema surrounding the known tibial plateau fracture with a bone contusion in the lateral femoral condyle.

7. large knee joint effusion.
